AMD's data center sales grew 97% in one year. The chipmaker reported $8.5 billion of data center revenue for the quarter on Tuesday, November 3.

AMD's total Q3 revenue hit a record $13.4 billion, up 45% from $9.2 billion a year ago, above the roughly $13.1 billion analysts expected (LSEG). Demand for its server chips and AI processors drove the jump, while gaming chip sales fell 40% to $773 million. AMD expects about $17 billion of revenue next quarter, above the $16.3 billion analysts expected (Bloomberg), and said it expects revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027. Shares rose 7.3% before the opening bell on Wednesday, November 4, Reuters reports, about $58 billion of value if the gains hold. Figures as of November 4, 2026.
